title: Enforce review separation using durable submission authorship
description: Implement the approved TASK-277 P0 integrity slice after TASK-274 preserves submission authorship. Add a canonical author identity that survives submission and owner reassignment, then key review claim and terminal review gates to that identity while preserving atomic duplicate-review arbitration. Existing submissions with unknown authorship must follow an explicit safe migration or escalation rule. Output sequencing: MAP_System/db/claims.py remains owned by TASK-274 and MAP_System/scripts/map_task.py remains owned by TASK-268. Register each deferred path with map_task.py add-output-path only after its predecessor releases, before editing that path.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical submission author identity survives SUBMITTED transitions, owner reassignment, rejection, rework, and resubmission without relying on reviewer-authored artifact text.
claim_review and approve or reject prevent the actual submission author from reviewing even when tasks.owner differs, while allowing a genuinely independent reviewer.
Legacy or open submissions with unknown author identity are handled by an explicit conservative migration or escalation rule; absence is never interpreted as proof of independence.
Atomic duplicate-review arbitration remains separate and unchanged in behavior, with race and owner-author-drift regression tests.
Focused lifecycle, mirror, event, and review validators pass and the delivery note records compatibility, rollback, and residual risk.
